🎵 Audio Preprocessing Exploration¶

This notebook allows you to visually inspect the 2D Mel-Spectrogram tensors generated by our new src/data/preprocessing.py script.

What you will see here:

  1. Loading the saved PyTorch .pt files.
  2. Inspecting the exact shape of the tensors (checking our math).
  3. Plotting individual sounds as 2D heatmaps (Time vs. Pitch).
  4. Plotting a grid of random sounds to see the visual variety in the dataset.
In [1]:
import os
import torch
import random
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from pathlib import Path

# Ensure we are pointing to the correct root directory
if Path.cwd().name == "notebooks":
    os.chdir("..")

PROCESSED_DIR = Path("data/processed")
pt_files = list(PROCESSED_DIR.glob("*.pt"))

print(f"✅ Found {len(pt_files)} processed tensor files.")
if len(pt_files) == 0:
    print("⚠️ No .pt files found! Run `python src/data/preprocessing.py` first.")

✅ Found 16291 processed tensor files.

1. Inspect a Single Tensor¶

Let's grab one random file and look at its shape and values. Because we set DURATION_SECONDS = 3, SAMPLE_RATE = 22050, and N_MELS = 80, we expect the tensor to look something like [1, 80, 258].

In [2]:
sample_file = random.choice(pt_files)
tensor = torch.load(sample_file)

print(f"File: {sample_file.name}")
print(f"Shape: {tensor.shape} -> [Channels, Mel-Bins, Time-Frames]")
print(f"Min Value: {tensor.min().item():.2f}")
print(f"Max Value: {tensor.max().item():.2f}")
print(f"Mean Value: {tensor.mean().item():.2f}")

File: item_010121_keyboard_electronic_002-097-100.pt
Shape: torch.Size([1, 80, 259]) -> [Channels, Mel-Bins, Time-Frames]
Min Value: -0.59
Max Value: 5.69
Mean Value: -0.00

2. Visualize a Mel-Spectrogram (The "Image" of Sound)¶

By plotting this 2D matrix using a colormap, we can see exactly what the neural network will see.

  • X-Axis: Time
  • Y-Axis: Pitch / Frequency (Mel Scale)
  • Color/Brightness: Volume / Amplitude
In [3]:
# Remove the channel dimension: [1, 80, T] -> [80, T]
spec2d = tensor.squeeze().numpy()

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 4))
plt.imshow(spec2d, origin='lower', aspect='auto', cmap='magma')
plt.colorbar(format='%+2.0f dB', label='Normalized Amplitude')
plt.title(f"Mel-Spectrogram: {sample_file.name}")
plt.xlabel("Time Frames")
plt.ylabel("Mel Frequency Bins")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

3. Grid of Random Samples¶

Let's pull 6 random sounds from the dataset to visually compare how a guitar note looks completely different from a vocal trill or a drum hit.

In [4]:
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(16, 8))
samples = random.sample(pt_files, 6)

for ax, file_path in zip(axes.flatten(), samples):
    t = torch.load(file_path)
    spec = t.squeeze().numpy()
    
    im = ax.imshow(spec, origin='lower', aspect='auto', cmap='magma')
    ax.set_title(file_path.name[:25] + "...", fontsize=10)
    ax.set_yticks([]) # Hide Y ticks for cleaner look
    ax.set_xticks([]) # Hide X ticks for cleaner look

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
